stories.completionNotes: Took the placeholder-injection path the AC named first: dashboard.html now carries __DEPLOY_VERSION__ and the state server substitutes it in _injectHtml, alongside the existing __SPLASH_TOKEN__ / __DISPLAY_AUTODIM__ / __DISPLAY_CAROUSEL__ seams. No JS reader was added -- one rule owns the chip. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: the version is read PER REQUEST, not cached at handler construction like the two config placeholders are. deploy-pi.sh restarts eclipse-states-http at step_install_state_server_units (line 1939) but stamps .deploy-version LAST at step_write_deploy_version (line 1955) -- deliberately, per US-354, so a failed restart cannot bump the stamp on a Pi still running old code. A start-time cache would therefore have rendered the PREVIOUS deploy's version on EVERY deploy: green tests, correct-looking code, and the exact stale literal the story exists to delete. Mutation-proved: caching at construction makes the chip read V0.29.23 after V0.29.24 was stamped, and only test_index_readsVersionPerRequest_notCachedAtStartup catches it. Cost is one small JSON read per HTML serve; the kiosk loads the page once. Honest degrade per AC#3: readDeployVersion returns None -- never a guess -- for no-path / absent / unreadable / malformed-JSON / missing / blank / non-string version, and the chip renders the SAME 'V?.?.?' sentinel the splash chip already uses, so one glyph means 'unknown build' on both surfaces. The placeholder is always substituted, so a raw __DEPLOY_VERSION__ can never reach the panel. NO deploy or unit-file change needed: --deploy-version-path defaults to '.deploy-version' (WorkingDirectory-relative, same trick as the existing --config, which ExecStart also does not pass), the service runs as mcornelison from the repo root with no sandboxing directives, and dashboard.html is already vouched in step_install_dashboard_assets so refresh_asset_dir will not prune it. 18 tests, 15 RED-first; the 3 markup guards were mutation-proved after the fact (baking a version literal trips 2, re-baking the dead sentinel trips 3). One test-quality note: the first cut of the no-dead-literal guard matched raw file text and tripped on my own explanatory HTML comment -- it now strips comments and asserts only on renderable markup. Green in-loop: tests/pi/splash + tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = exit 0; ruff clean. FILE:// PREVIEW CAVEAT for Iris: an un-substituted preview shows the raw __DEPLOY_VERSION__ text in the chip rather than a pretty sentinel -- the quoted-placeholder trick the two config seams use does not apply to HTML text content. Deliberate: unmistakably 'not substituted', and dev-only. OWED: the on-Pi read of the header chip after deploy (chip must show the real V0.29.xx) -- PM/CIO drill, not codeable.

Note filed to Atlas for the one contract delta (below); no BLOCK, no wait -- if he NAKs a preferred seam the DoD is unchanged ('tile reflects the real source') per conditionalOutcomes. ROOT confirmed as written: _gatherPowerSource now reads PowerSourceProvider (X1209 GPIO6 PLD) direct, and PowerMonitor is REMOVED from that path entirely -- a second acquisition path could disagree with GPIO6, which is the SSOT violation the design gate forbids. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: the new PowerSourceProvider.isAvailable property is the only contract change, and it exists because the sequencer's safe direction is a LIE on a display. An unreadable PLD deliberately answers isExternalPowerPresent()==True (never self-brick on a dead signal); taking that at face value on the tile paints a confident lit-green 'external' off a DEAD GPIO -- strictly worse than the gray bolt this story exists to fix. So the provider exposes the FACT (is the line readable) and each consumer keeps its OWN uncertainty policy: sequencer=treat-as-present, UI=unknown. isExternalPowerPresent/isPowerLost/startupArmCheck are untouched, so the shutdown path cannot have moved. Pinned by test_gatherPowerState_providerBuiltAfterEmitterInit_isStillRead. 17 tests, 5 mutations all caught (drop the isAvailable gate / vocab drift external->ac / capture-at-init / drop the exception guard / re-add the PowerMonitor path). stories.title: Idle-card clock to 12-hour AM/PM
acceptance: fmtClock (carousel.js:1929) renders 12-hour time with an AM/PM meridiem (mod-12 with 12 for noon/midnight), not getHours() 24-hour
minutes stay zero-padded; no seconds unless already shown
purely a format change -- no data source touched; ruff/lint clean in-loop

stories.goal: As the operator, I want the idle-home clock in 12-hour AM/PM format instead of 24-hour, matching how I read time at a glance.
stories.completionNotes: fmtClock now renders 12-hour AM/PM: mod-12 with 12 restored for midnight/noon, BARE hour ('2:05 PM', never '02:05 PM'), zero-padded minute, no seconds. Pure format change -- no data source, no state file, no emitter touched, and the Date still comes from the caller. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: I MOVED fmtClock (and its two() padding helper) out of the browser-only `if (typeof document !== 'undefined')` block up into the pure/exported section. That was not a preference -- under 'use strict' an ES6 function declaration inside a block is BLOCK-SCOPED, so fmtClock was structurally unreachable from the api export literal and from every test; hoisting does not rescue it. It was always pure (it formats the Date it is handed; it never reads a clock), so the block comment's 'the pure view logic stays clock-free, so these live in the DOM layer' rationale was true of fmtDate but never of fmtClock. fmtDate + IDLE_DAYS/IDLE_MONTHS deliberately stayed put -- out of scope. There is now exactly ONE clock formatter in carousel.js; the DOM block CALLS it and does not own one, and the source comment there says so to stop a future edit re-declaring a local. 10 tests, all 10 RED first (the DOM one failed on the real rendered value '22:50' -- the actual bug, not a proxy). 3 mutations proved: bare `% 12` without the `|| 12` restore -> midnight+noon+sweep fail; meridiem boundary `h <= 12` -> noon reads AM, caught by 2; RE-SHADOWING the DOM block with the old 24-hour fmtClock -> ALL NINE fmtClock unit tests stay green and ONLY the end-to-end DOM test catches it. That third one is why the story has an end-to-end test at all: it is the exact US-494/US-499/US-502 shape where both halves are individually correct and simply do not agree. Needed a dedicated probe (tests/ui/idle_clock_probe.js) because carousel_probe.js JSON-decodes its arguments and JSON has no Date -- it would hand fmtClock a Number and the formatter would read NaN; the probe builds the Date from local calendar COMPONENTS so the fixture is the clock FACE, not an instant, and the assertions hold in any timezone. Green in-loop: tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 580 passed, exit 0 (the 10 new ones verified RUN not skipped, node present); ruff clean. Not run in-loop per TD-059: full pytest + mypy -- but this touches ONE JS function and no Python source, so the regression risk is confined to the UI suite that already ran whole. FLAG FOR THE ON-PI DRILL (layout, not logic): .idle-header is a flex row (wordmark + clock + date, gap 8px) on the 480px design stage, and the clock string grew ~3 glyphs ('22:05' -> '10:05 PM'). I did NOT pre-emptively touch dashboard.css -- the render harness resolves CSS but does not do text metrics, so any tightening would have been a guess at a panel I cannot see. If the header crowds on the real 480x320 panel, that is a one-line CSS follow-up. OWED: the on-Pi read of the idle-card clock at a known time -- PM/CIO drill, not codeable.

stories.title: Battery Health writer: a PRODUCTION drain-event writer (battery_health_log gets new rows again)
acceptance: [CARVED from US-504 per its own conditionalOutcome. Sibling US-504b (verdict producer) is DONE -- it consumes runtime_seconds/timestamps/load_class only and never reads vcell/soc, so this story was NOT blocking it.]

[ROOT -- corrected mechanism] BatteryHealthRecorder.startDrainEvent/endDrainEvent already write start_vcell_v/end_vcell_v/start_soc_pct/end_soc_pct correctly, and scripts/record_drain_test.py populates them. What does not exist is ANY production caller in src/ -- the US-216 auto-open path was retired under US-442/TD-058 and nothing replaced it. Consequence: no running Pi ever writes a battery_health_log row, so the card reads 'unknown' PERMANENTLY, not 'until fresh drains exist'. Build the production writer.

on a real AC->BATTERY transition a drain-event row is opened carrying a REAL start_vcell_v + start_soc_pct read from the MAX17048; on BATTERY->AC (or at cutoff shutdown) it is closed with a real end_vcell_v + end_soc_pct and a real runtime_seconds. Honest-instrument: an unreadable gauge or an uncalibrated SoC register writes NULL, never a guessed number (reuse readCalibratedRegisterSocPct + its cold-start window).

[SEAM] PowerMonitor.onTransition is the existing registration point and PowerMonitor already receives the GPIO6 truth via the US-502 _PowerSourceUiBridge sink (lifecycle.py ~2250). Read the UPS LATE-BOUND, at transition time, not captured at construction (US-501/502/503 all hit the boot-order trap this sprint).

[ORPHAN POLICY -- NEEDS A RULING BEFORE BUILD] US-442 requires a production writer to open+close as a single unit OR guarantee the close on the shutdown path -- but the drain most worth measuring is the one that ENDS in a cutoff shutdown, exactly where a deferred close is most likely to be lost. Options: (A) open-at-loss + close-at-restore-or-shutdown + boot reaper; (B) single INSERT at close, drain held in memory (zero orphans, but a hard crash loses the row entirely); (C) A with the ShutdownSequencer close primary and the reaper as backstop. Ralph recommends (C). See offices/pm/inbox/2026-08-02-from-ralph-us504-carved-504a-writer-504b-producer.md

[LOAD-BEARING TRAP] if a boot reaper is built, it MUST NOT close orphans via endDrainEvent -- that computes runtime_seconds from the timestamp delta, which across a reboot manufactures a runtime spanning the whole downtime, clears the 600s gate, and poisons the verdict median with a fabricated multi-hour 'drain'. The reaper stamps end_timestamp and leaves runtime_seconds NULL so the row can never qualify.

test proves: a simulated AC->BATTERY->AC cycle writes ONE row with real vcell/soc at both ends; an unreadable gauge writes NULL not a guess; the shutdown path closes an open drain; a reaped orphan carries NULL runtime_seconds and does NOT qualify in the US-504b verdict. ruff clean in-loop
does NOT delay, block, or add a failure mode to the ShutdownSequencer -- the drain close is best-effort and can never keep the Pi from powering off (I-038 lesson)

validationCriteria.outcome: a NEW row exists for that window with non-NULL start_vcell_v/start_soc_pct/end_vcell_v/end_soc_pct and a real runtime_seconds; no orphan row is left behind across a reboot

If he moves to a depth/cutoff-reached gate, THIS writer is what has to record that signal -- so his answer changes what gets written. Filed 2026-08-02 to offices/tuner/inbox/.

stories.title: Battery Health truthfulness: remove no-source TEMP + HEALTH verdict + last-health-check (Spool spec)
acceptance: [SEQUENCING] wires the BATTERY portion of the consolidated 'Health' card (US-507, landed Sprint 68 / V0.29.23). REMOVE the TEMP tile (MAX17048 has NO temp register) but KEEP the ambient_temp_c column (a future BMP390 baro fills it -- Spool). Keep CELL(volts)+CHARGE(%) as-is (real MAX17048).

[HEALTH VERDICT PRODUCER -- Spool [EXACT] spec] source = battery_health_log (NOT a live MAX17048 spot read -- capacity fade needs runtime-to-cutoff). Qualifying row gate: end_timestamp NOT NULL AND load_class='production' AND runtime_seconds >= [EXACT:600]. RUNTIME_BASELINE_S=[EXACT:727]. States on median of last 3 qualifying drains: good >= [EXACT:80]% baseline (>=582s) | degraded 60-80% (436-582s) | replace < [EXACT:60]% (<436s) | unknown = default (< 3 qualifying in trailing [EXACT:180] days OR any required input NULL). median-of-3 (not last-1: single-drain scatter +-15%).

[LAST-HEALTH-CHECK] = MAX(start_timestamp) over qualifying rows only (a partial/aborted drain is NOT a health check). If last check > [EXACT:90] days old, FORCE verdict to unknown regardless of numbers (stale health data is not health data).

[SEVERITY -- Spool] 🟢 INFORMATIONAL at every state incl 'replace' -- NEVER alarm-red, never owns the screen, never competes with coolant/DTC-STOP on a driving surface (UPS margin is ~12min vs <1min needed = 10x; 'replace' = data-integrity margin thinned, not a car risk).

[HONEST END-STATE] accept the card legitimately reads 'unknown' + last-check '2026-05-16' until fresh qualifying drains exist -- THAT IS THE INSTRUMENT WORKING, not a bug. Test proves the qualifying-gate + median-of-3 + 90-day override + honest-unknown-on-NULL; ruff clean.

validationCriteria.outcome: verdict computed only from qualifying rows via median-of-3 vs the 727s baseline; forces 'unknown' on <3 qualifying / any NULL / >90-day-stale; last-health-check ignores partial drains; renders 🟢 never red; no TEMP tile

conditionalOutcomes: [EXACT:] values (600/727/80/60/180/90) are Spool load-bearing -- flag Spool before any drift
stories.goal: As the operator, I want every battery field on a real source (or absent), so the card is honest -- no 'no source' temp, and a HEALTH verdict grounded in real capacity data rather than a manufactured value or a hardcoded 'unknown'.
stories.completionNotes: US-504 CARVED into US-504a (writer) + this (producer) on the story's own conditionalOutcome -- it grew, and the writer half turned out to be a different, larger animal (see US-504a + the PM note). Every Spool [EXACT] value implemented verbatim, none drifted: 600 gate / 727 baseline / 80-60 bands / 180-day window / 90-day staleness / median-of-3. THE ONE CALL THE PM SHOULD KNOW ABOUT: AC2 called the writer-fix a BLOCKING sub-story on the grounds that 'without this the verdict has nothing to consume' -- that premise is wrong. Spool's own verdict spec reads start_timestamp/end_timestamp/runtime_seconds/load_class and never touches vcell or soc, so the producer was fully buildable without it and is now built + green. That is why this half landed first rather than stalling behind a story that needs two rulings. THE SPEC BUG WORTH THE MOST ATTENTION (filed to Spool 2026-08-02): the qualifying gate (runtime_seconds >= 600) sits entirely ABOVE both sub-good bands (degraded 436-582s, replace <436s). Every row that survives the gate is >=600s therefore >=582s therefore always 'good' -- so through the real pipeline degraded and replace are UNREACHABLE, and a pack that genuinely dies at 500s is filtered out as a 'partial drain' rather than reported as degraded. The verdict silently cannot degrade; it fails safe toward reassurance, the wrong direction for an honest instrument. Implemented VERBATIM anyway (both numbers are [EXACT] Spool values -- flag, never drift), with the bands isolated in a public verdictForMedianRuntime() so the mapping stays fully exercised by tests and only the gate constant has to move when he rules. SECOND CORRECTION for the record: AC2's 'nothing populates start_vcell_v/end_vcell_v/start_soc_pct/end_soc_pct' is right at the data and wrong at the mechanism -- the recorder writes all four correctly and the bench CLI uses them; there is simply ZERO production caller in src/ since US-442/TD-058 retired the auto-open path. So no running Pi writes ANY row, and the card reads 'unknown' permanently rather than 'until fresh drains exist'. That is US-504a. HONEST-INSTRUMENT throughout: unknown is the DEFAULT, never a swallowed failure -- absent DB, unreadable log, unparseable clock, <3 qualifying rows in the trailing 180 days, or a >90-day-stale last check all resolve to unknown, and the staleness override is checked BEFORE the numbers so a stale reading can never paint a confident verdict of any colour. Today that override fires (newest qualifying row 2026-05-16, 78 days) -- the card correctly reads unknown + 2026-05-16, which is the instrument working. ONE VOCABULARY END-TO-END: the old green/attn/low display tiers were a SECOND enum for the same fact (the cross-module enum-identity class that cost the 9-drain saga) and are RETIRED -- battery_health_emitter now re-exports the producer's good/degraded/replace/unknown rather than declaring its own, and carousel.js healthLevel/healthValue speak those words. Severity per Spool: good->ok, degraded AND replace->neutral, unrecognised->unavailable. 'replace' is deliberately NOT red (the UPS carries ~12min against the <1min a clean shutdown needs -- a thinned data-integrity margin is not a car risk) and deliberately NOT ok either (that would claim health the data does not support); neutral is the only tier that neither alarms nor reassures. TEMP tile REMOVED -- the MAX17048 register map has no temperature at all, so the tile rendered 'not captured' on every row ever logged; the ambient_temp_c COLUMN stays for the BMP390. Verdict read is LAZY per emit via getattr, not captured at emitter construction -- the boot-order trap this sprint has now hit in US-501, US-502 and here; it also means a drain recorded while the orchestrator runs reaches the card without a restart. Green in-loop: tests/pi/power + tests/pi/orchestrator + tests/pi/splash/test_battery_health_emitter.py + tests/ui + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 913 passed, exit 0; ruff clean on all 11 touched files (2 import-sort fixes applied). NOT run in-loop per TD-059: full pytest + mypy -- card_state_emitter.py is a base-module touch for the SECOND time this sprint (US-502 was the first), so prioritise the full-suite regression at close. OWED: the seeded-row read of the Health card on the Pi -- PM/CIO drill, not codeable.

stories.title: Gyro-fused pitch for states/imu (complementary/Madgwick + ZUPT) -- honest grade + altitude foundation
acceptance: the states/imu pitch (the gradePct source) is GYRO-FUSED (complementary or Madgwick): gyro integrated for short-term, accel corrects the gyro ONLY when |accel| is near 1 g (Spool). gyro-alone drifts; accel-alone is contaminated by longitudinal g; neither works standalone

[ZUPT] zero-velocity bias update: at every confirmed stop (OBD speed 0 for > [EXACT:3] s) the accel reads pure gravity -> measured tilt = true chassis pitch; average over stops to converge the pitch BIAS out (valid because Chicagoland terrain is flat -> real slopes average ~0). city stoplights are the free calibration signal

the fused pitch feeds gradePct (the honest grade on US-508) AND is the prerequisite the future interim altitude (US-519) integrates -- publish it in states/imu per Atlas's DELTA-2 contract; raw accel/gyro stay on the EDR bus
[SPOOL SIZING -- route him] send Spool the current pitch derivation + the pitch/speed sample rates so he sizes expected sigma_pitch BEFORE the altitude display (US-519/520) builds on it
test proves: a longitudinal 0.3 g on flat ground does NOT produce a ~16.7-degree pitch (the failure mode); ZUPT converges the bias over simulated stops; ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: on the Pi: apply/simulate a longitudinal 0.3 g on flat ground, then a confirmed stop on a known slope
validationCriteria.outcome: pitch stays ~0 under pure acceleration (not 16.7 deg); at the stop, pitch reads the true chassis tilt; grade on US-508 is no longer accel-contaminated

conditionalOutcomes: if the current grade/pitch is already gyro-fused (verify first), this narrows to adding ZUPT + confirming the fusion; [EXACT:3]s ZUPT gate is Spool load-bearing
stories.goal: As the grade + (future) altitude signals, I want pitch from a gyro-accel fusion, not accel-only tilt, so a 0.3 g acceleration isn't misread as a 16.7-degree climb (Spool: an accelerometer cannot distinguish grade from acceleration -- they are the same measurement).
